html:
Nationwide protests in South Korea in June 1987 that forced the military regime of Chun Doo-hwan to accept direct elections for president.

Anger had built since the Gwangju Uprising of 1980. In January 1987 a student, Park Jong-chul, died under police torture, and the government tried to hide it. In June, Chun named his ally Roh Tae-woo as his successor under the old indirect system. Students, workers and office workers then filled the streets of Seoul and other cities for weeks. A student, Lee Han-yeol, was struck by a tear gas canister and later died.

With the Seoul Olympics coming and the world watching, Roh announced on 29 June that the regime would accept direct elections and other reforms. In the December election the opposition split between Kim Young-sam and Kim Dae-jung, and Roh won. Still, the protests are seen as the moment South Korea became a democracy.
sum: Nationwide protests in South Korea in June 1987 that forced the military regime of Chun Doo-hwan to accept direct elections for president.
